solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Giving away ending, scatty English lady ruins exciting detective story

indicators.note: to excite is to stir up, so these letters are stirred into a new order
giving away its ending tells us to drop the final letter of the word scatty

parts.note: taken as written before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A scatterbrained Englishwoman spoils a thriller by blurting out how it ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving away ending' takes the Y off SCATTY, leaving SCATT; with E, LADY and RUINS, 'exciting' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the first Sherlock Holmes novel by Conan Doyle, an example of a detective story.

clue.text: State troopers perhaps breaking into song

indicators.note: the soldiers break into the song, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera
troopers are soldiers, an example of men in the military sense

explanation.surface: Soldiers suddenly burst out singing, perhaps a patriotic tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Armenia is a sovereign country in the Caucasus, so an example of a state.

clue.text: Woman is detained in Mediterranean port to intimidate

indicators.note: being detained means being held inside, so the woman and IS go inside the port

parts.note: Tyre is an ancient port on the coast of Lebanon
Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman held at a Levantine port is meant to frighten someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To tyrannise is to rule or treat cruelly, bullying people into submission, close in sense to intimidating them.

clue.text: House in Ireland takes year to get cleaner

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: An Irish household engages a cleaner on a yearly contract.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dail (Dáil Éireann) is Ireland's parliamentary chamber, a 'House' as in House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a daily is a domestic help who comes in each day to clean.

clue.text: Dine and be almost ill, cooking being this?

definitions.text: Dine and be almost ill, cooking being this?

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are mixed up like ingredients
almost means not quite all of the word ill, so its last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written before it is cut short

explanation.surface: Someone eats a meal and nearly throws up, wondering whether the cooking was to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts ILL to IL; 'cooking' rearranges DINE, BE and IL. The whole clue also describes food bad enough to make a diner ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that nearly makes a diner sick is unfit to be eaten, the meaning of the word.

clue.text: Small curtsey regularly is a show of respect

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the two words, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A little bob of the knee counts as a polite gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes letters 1, 3, 5... across 'Small curtsey', not a curtsey from one word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A salute is a gesture of greeting or honour, such as a raised hand to the brow.

clue.text: Annoy, for example replacing Bible for mass

indicators.note: replacing means one pair of letters takes the place of another in the word

parts.note: to aggravate is, informally, to annoy
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
eg is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Annoyance arises when an example is swapped for scripture at church mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' puts EG where AV stood in AGGRAVATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aggregate is a total or whole formed by combining parts, a mass of things gathered together.

clue.text: Game could be tight after getting bowled out

indicators.note: out means the letter for bowled is taken away from the word

parts.note: tight and blotto are both slang for drunk
b is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A cricket match where a batsman, once dismissed, ends up drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowled out' sounds like a dismissal in cricket, but it removes B from BLOTTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a lottery-style numbers game, a form of bingo played for prizes.

clue.text: One's in charge of convicts, note, in the middle of bird

indicators.note: the note sits in the middle of the bird, splitting it

parts.note: a turkey is a bird

explanation.surface: A prison warden is jotted down amid talk of a bird, which is also slang for jail time.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnkey is an old word for a jailer, who held the keys and guarded prisoners.

clue.text: Spoil little child? It produces strongly conflicting opinions!

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: Should one indulge a toddler? Parents argue fiercely about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Marmite is a British yeast-extract spread, advertised as 'love it or hate it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The spread's own slogan made its name a byword for anything that divides people sharply.

clue.text: One illuminates boat relatively easily

definitions.meaning: a device that makes a flame, as for a cigarette
a flat-bottomed barge for unloading ships
comparative of light in the sense of effortless, more easily

explanation.surface: Something lit up a boat with little trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: a flame-making gadget, a barge, and the comparative of light meaning less heavy or easier.

clue.text: Old woman's extremely nasty to nurse

parts.note: nan is an informal word for a grandmother

indicators.note: extremely means taking the word nasty's extreme letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A grandmother is very unpleasant to the nurse looking after her.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny is a children's nurse employed to look after a family's young.

clue.text: Cook in chaotic kitchen is facing criticism

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
chaotic means the letters of kitchen are thrown into disorder

parts.note: to do food is to cook it

explanation.surface: A chef working in a disorderly kitchen gets told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like the subject of the sentence; it is the verb DO (as in 'do the vegetables'), and 'chaotic' and 'in' are its instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally standing trial in court; figuratively, being blamed or criticised.

clue.text: Friendly, retaining cordiality for a start?

definitions.text: Friendly, retaining cordiality for a start?

indicators.note: retaining means holding inside, so the word for friendly holds the letter

parts.note: amiable means friendly

indicators.note: for a start means the first letter of cordiality

explanation.surface: Someone stays pleasant, keeping things cordial, at least at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friendly' works twice: it is the definition and also AMIABLE, which 'retaining' wraps round C.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable means showing goodwill, as in an amicable divorce; a near-synonym of friendly.

clue.text: Fairly slow at nightclub initially? One can gatecrash party

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of at and nightclub
gatecrashers get inside a party uninvited, so these pieces go inside it

parts.note: a do is a party
an is the indefinite article, meaning one
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Things are fairly slow at the club early on, until someone with a drink barges into the party.
explanation.definitionFit: Andantino is a musical tempo marking, slightly quicker than andante, a moderate walking pace.

clue.text: Listener solver's lacking refinement

parts.note: the ear is the organ that listens
thy is an old form of your, the solver being addressed as you

explanation.surface: A solver of the Listener crossword is called unsophisticated.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener is a famously hard British crossword series, which makes 'Listener' look like a proper name.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is crude or coarse, so earthy means lacking refinement.

clue.text: Put vehicle back on board? That's easily managed

indicators.note: back means the word for vehicle runs backwards

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Putting a toy car back on the game board is no trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Tractable describes someone or something docile and easy to control or handle.

clue.text: Sons order four Wagner operas, getting less Brahms and Liszt

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
the OBE is the Order of the British Empire
Wagner's Ring cycle is four operas

explanation.surface: Sons book a Wagner cycle, having had enough of Brahms and Liszt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brahms and Liszt' is Cockney rhyming slang for pissed, meaning drunk, so the composers mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sobering up is to become less drunk, which the rhyming slang describes.

clue.text: Set programme and finish off in the oven

indicators.note: in puts the finish inside the oven

parts.note: an Aga is a British range cooker with ovens
to finish off is to end

explanation.surface: A recipe's step: follow the plan, then finish cooking in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a heavy cast-iron stove found in British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items to be dealt with, as at a meeting: a fixed schedule.

clue.text: What live music venue often has to give up

definitions.text: What live music venue often has
definitions.meaning: split as a phrase, a performing group on stage
to quit or desert something entirely

explanation.definitionFit: To abandon a plan is to give it up; read as three words, a club often has musicians playing.

clue.text: Chap, a colonist, comprehends New Testament

indicators.note: comprehends means takes in, so the letter for new is held within

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a chap
an ant lives in a colony

explanation.surface: A man, a settler, understands the New Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Testament' looks like one phrase; 'New' is wordplay and 'Testament' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament in the biblical sense is a covenant, a solemn agreement between God and people.

clue.text: In which things are done to hide attempt to capture queen

definitions.text: In which things are done to hide

indicators.note: to capture is to hold within, so the queen goes inside the attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
Anne was a queen of Great Britain

explanation.surface: Something is done in secret in an effort to seize the queen, as in a chess game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' is an animal skin, not concealment.
explanation.definitionFit: A tannery is the works where animal skins are treated and turned into leather.

clue.text: Amazed Nigel Short cracked Azed barred puzzle?

indicators.note: cracked means the letters are broken up and reassembled
barred means the word Azed is kept out of Amazed
short means the name Nigel loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before it is cut

explanation.surface: Chess grandmaster Nigel Short astonishingly solved one of Azed's barred crosswords.
explanation.walkthrough: Azed is the Observer's barred-grid crossword setter. 'barred' leaves AM from AMAZED; 'Short' gives NIGE; 'cracked' rearranges AM and NIGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or riddle, something baffling.

clue.text: One scans a Byzantine poetic device

indicators.note: Byzantine means intricate and convoluted, so the letters are tangled

explanation.surface: Someone analyses the metre of a Byzantine poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Assonance is the echo of vowel sounds in nearby words, a technique used in verse.

clue.text: Wrote some letters in order to get wheat

definitions.meaning: put the letters of a word down correctly, past tense
a hardy ancient grain related to wheat

explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of spell, and also an old cereal grain, a type of wheat.

clue.text: What mountaineer may use around peak? That's feasible

indicators.note: around means the word for peak is turned round

parts.note: a tip is a peak or summit
something that is on is feasible, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: A climber wonders whether a route round the summit is possible.
explanation.definitionFit: A piton is a metal spike hammered into rock to anchor a climbing rope.

clue.text: Board aircraft second to last

indicators.note: the second letter is taken to the last position in the word

parts.note: a plane is an aircraft

explanation.surface: Get on the plane, the next-to-last passenger to do so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second to last' reads as the penultimate; it means the second letter goes to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel is a board, either a flat sheet or a group of people like a board of judges.

clue.text: Daughter's scratching head, appearing to be thinking

indicators.note: scratching out the head means dropping the first letter

parts.note: appearing and seeming are synonyms

explanation.surface: A daughter scratches her head, looking deep in thought.
explanation.definitionFit: To deem is to judge or consider, so deeming means thinking something to be so.

clue.text: Returning soldier faces arrest, having abandoned British base

indicators.note: faces means comes in front of what follows
returning means the soldier's letters run backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: abandoning the letter for British drops it from the word

parts.note: to nobble is slang for to seize or arrest

explanation.surface: A soldier coming home faces arrest after deserting a British base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a military base; it means low and dishonourable.
explanation.definitionFit: Base as an adjective means morally low, a synonym of dishonourable.

clue.text: Art — Goya, nothing less — all in one large building here?

definitions.text: Art — Goya, nothing less — all in one large building here?

indicators.note: building means putting the letters together in a new structure
less means the letter for nothing is taken from Goya

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Paintings including Goya's, all gathered in one big gallery in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes O from GOYA; 'building' rearranges ART, GYA, ALLINONE and L. The whole clue also describes the place: the London gallery holds Goya's portraits.
explanation.definitionFit: The National Gallery on Trafalgar Square is a large building housing art, including works by Goya.
